bib.title: LLM.int8(): 8-bit Matrix Multiplication for Transformers at Scale
bib.venue: 36th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2022)

read.skipped: reference list skimmed only; checklist pages skimmed

question: Can multi-billion-parameter transformers be quantized to Int8 for inference without any performance degradation, and why do standard 8-bit methods fail at scale?
hypothesis: Emergent, systematic large-magnitude outlier feature dimensions cause quantization failure beyond about 6.7B parameters; isolating them in 16-bit while quantizing the rest vector-wise should remove the degradation.
contributions: Vector-wise Int8 quantization with separate normalization constants per inner product
Mixed-precision decomposition: outlier feature dimensions multiplied in 16-bit, other 99.9% in 8-bit
Analysis of emergent outlier features (phase shift at 6.7B, tied to perplexity), with their effect on attention and perplexity
Open-source bitsandbytes software and Hugging Face Transformers integration

method.summary: LLM.int8() combines absmax vector-wise Int8 quantization (row constants for X, column constants for W, dequantized by their outer product) with mixed-precision decomposition: input feature dimensions with any value of magnitude >= 6.0 are multiplied in FP16, the rest in Int8 with Int32 accumulation. Applied to feed-forward and attention projection layers of pretrained models without further training; evaluated by C4 perplexity (125M-13B fairseq models) and zeroshot accuracy (OPT 125M-175B).

parameters.outlier_analysis_criteria: magnitude >= 6.0, in the same feature dim in >= 25% of layers, and >= 6% of sequence dimensions

results.claim: At 13B, LLM.int8() matches 32-bit C4 perplexity while Int8 absmax degrades sharply.
results.setup: fairseq 13B, C4 validation, Absmax LLM.int8() (vector-wise + decomp)
results.table: Table 1, row Absmax LLM.int8() (vector-wise + decomp), column 13B

results.claim: Zeropoint vector-wise without decomposition degrades at 13B.
results.table: Table 1, row Int8 zeropoint vector-wise, column 13B

results.claim: Memory footprint of BLOOM-176B reduced by 1.96x.
results.quote: For example, for BLOOM-176B, we reduce the memory footprint of the model by 1.96x.

results.claim: Outlier features appear in all layers abruptly between 6B and 6.7B parameters.
results.setup: fairseq/GPT-2/GPT-J models up to 13B; outliers magnitude >= 6, >= 25% layers, >= 6% sequence dims
results.quote: occurs suddenly between 6B and 6.7B parameters as shown in Figure 3a as the percentage of layers affected increases from 65% to 100%

results.claim: About 150k outliers per sequence at 6.7B concentrated in 6 feature dimensions.
results.quote:
At the 6.7B scale, 150,000 outliers occur
per sequence, but they are concentrated in only 6 feature dimensions across the entire transformer.
results.note: Section 4.2 says 'about 150k outliers features per sequence' and body text of Section 4 intro says up to 150k per 2048-token sequence for a 13B model

results.claim: Zeroing outlier dimensions raises perplexity 600-1000% while removing random dimensions raises it about 0.1%.
results.setup: outlier dims set to zero, at most 7 dims, ~0.1% of features
results.quote: validation perplexity increases by 600-1000% even though there are at most 7 outlier feature dimensions

results.claim: Removing outliers cuts mean top-1 attention softmax probability from about 40% to about 20%.
results.setup: per-layer independent removal, outlier dims zeroed
results.quote:
the mean top-1
softmax probability is reduced from about 40% to about 20%

results.claim: Raw Int8 matmul is 2x faster only at large size; with quantization overhead, LLM.int8() is slower for small models and 1.81x at 175B-size dimension.
results.setup: first FFN layer of GPT-3 175B (model dim 12288)
results.table: Table 5, row LLM.int8() (vector-wise+decomp), column 175B (1.81x); 0.14x at Small

results.claim: Int8 fine-tuning of FFN only gives no degradation on GLUE (vector-wise mean 88.81 vs 88.61 32-bit).
Int8 training with 8-bit FFN plus attention projections degrades at 1.1B LM (PPL 10.52 vs 9.99).
results.setup: 1.1B LM, FFN and linear attention in 8-bit, no decomposition

limits: Only the Int8 data type studied, not FP8.
Only models up to 175B studied; additional emergent properties might disrupt quantization at larger scales.
Int8 not used for the attention function (no parameters); left for future work.
Focuses on inference; training and fine-tuning only an initial analysis in Appendix E and F.
Quantization overhead slows inference for models under 6.7B; primary aim is memory, not speed.
Perplexity comparison across baselines covers only 125M to 13B; larger scales only via OPT zeroshot accuracy (Figure 1).
Hyperparameters of the Int8 training and fine-tuning experiments are not given.

terms.definition: assign a separate scaling constant to each row of X and each column of W, and dequantize by the outer product of the constants
outlier feature dimensions (magnitude >= alpha = 6.0) are multiplied in 16-bit, the other dimensions in 8-bit
